title: What later audits say happened to earlier questioned costs
question: Which earlier findings led to payments, later approval or a documented control change?
finding: 11 selected San Francisco recipients have paired audit reports. The table identifies the exact amount reviewed, the action taken and where the follow-up appears.
how: Compare the initial signed report to the following audit for the same recipient and read the cited prior-finding schedule or financial note. Cross-check programs, fiscal periods and entities before adding amounts.
limits: A corrected procedure can coexist with a separate unresolved monetary decision. This selection includes only the identified findings and gives no portfolio-wide estimate of repayments.

rows.issue: $204,379 in meal overpayments and $27,189 in separate attendance claims.
rows.outcome: The audited schedule records $100,470 repaid in FY2016 and $131,098 in FY2017. The remaining balance on both programs was zero at June 30, 2017.

rows.issue: The audit questioned $400,000 under Treasury award 151FA013659 because compensation lacked timekeeping support. The financial and federal references describe the same weakness.
rows.outcome: The FY2017 prior-finding schedule reports the same two references together and records a new tracking tool and compliance position. It marks the finding corrected. The schedule does not document repayment or disallowance.

rows.issue: A missing identity document led to $10,467 in questioned student aid. The work-study payroll finding concerned a different issue.
rows.outcome: Auditors verified the student’s ID and eligibility and reported no remaining questioned costs on the identity finding. The work-study review found errors for 22 of 90 students. The institute documented $460 paid to seven underpaid students and $659 returned to the program for 15 overpayments.

rows.entity: City and County of San Francisco
rows.issue: The City removed $6,081,362 in federal claims for disaster response costs initially outside the dates of three awards.
rows.outcome: The FY2021 audit records corrective action and retroactive amendments extending the eligible periods to cover the expenses. The auditor considered the original timing issue obsolete.

rows.issue: The college used the wrong indirect-cost rate and included lost revenue in its expense base. Auditors questioned $427,867 of college pandemic aid.
rows.outcome: The FY2022 schedule marks the review procedure implemented. It does not identify a refund or final federal disallowance.

rows.issue: Two findings cite the same $161,786 of commercial rent, involving an assignment of leases and the appointment of an affiliated management agent without advance HUD approval.
rows.outcome: The FY2023 schedule says HUD retroactively approved the assignment, appointment and payment of $161,786 to the affiliate. The balance must not be counted twice or recorded as an outstanding federal loss.

rows.issue: About $6,800 in personal card charges appeared in the financial and federal sections through an explicit cross-reference.
rows.outcome: The next report records the site manager’s dismissal and restricted card access. It gives no amount later collected. The vacancy and inspection finding was separate and carried no questioned costs.

rows.issue: The auditor questioned $55,070 in fringe benefits and shared costs charged to a federal maternal and child health grant without adjustments based on actual costs.
rows.outcome: The FY2023 schedule marks the finding corrected. The status entry does not establish the amount, if any, returned to the funder.

rows.issue: Two employee allocations overcharged a rehabilitation grant by $3,227 and $865. The combined $4,092 was questioned.
rows.outcome: The FY2024 report says the monitoring recommendation took effect July 1, 2023 and reports no similar FY2024 finding. The status entry does not document collection of the $4,092.

rows.entity: Centers for Equity and Success, Inc.
rows.issue: The Labor Department questioned $5,560 in YouthBuild participant costs and separately requested the calculation for shared expenses.
rows.outcome: The grantee reported adjusting the costs in December 2023. Its FY2024 audit cites a July 23, 2024 Labor Department letter that closed all nine findings.

rows.entity: Bay Area Air Quality Management District
rows.issue: Eight staffing charges that exceeded contract terms overstated costs by $9,316 on the federal BioWatch grant.
rows.outcome: The FY2025 audit marks the recommendation implemented. Its prior-finding schedule gives no amount or date of a refund or credit.
